youtube.aciklama: In an example of posterior canal BPPV, on the right Dix-Hallpike the nystagmus starts after a latency of about three seconds; the fast phase beats upward, toward the forehead, and in the torsional part the upper pole of the eye beats toward the lower, right ear. The nystagmus first builds, then fades, and dies out in about twenty seconds; on sitting up, a brief, weaker nystagmus in the opposite direction is seen. This course is typical of canalithiasis; the diagnosis is made by the physician.
